dedupe_keys.name: inunda gpu native differentiable flood inundation solver

description: Inunda is a GPU-native, differentiable solver for high-resolution flood inundation, described in a July 2026 arXiv paper by Zhi Li. It solves the two-dimensional shallow water equations with a mass-conservative local-inertial scheme and runs multi-day events over millions of cells in minutes on a single GPU; because each operator supports automatic differentiation, parameters can be calibrated by gradient descent against gage observations. Three cases are shown: a Hurricane Harvey hindcast in Harris County, Texas, matching surveyed high-water marks with a mean absolute error of 0.67 m and a median gage Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of +0.72 against +0.31 for the operational National Water Model version 3.0; a probabilistic forecast for the July 2025 Central Texas flash flood driven by an 18-member convection-allowing rainfall ensemble; and a post-fire flash flood in the Rio Ruidoso burn scar where calibration recovers the spatial field of saturated hydraulic conductivity. Coverage: any domain with terrain and forcing, demonstrated in Texas and New Mexico. Access: an open pipeline is claimed in the abstract; the code location and licence were not read; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Caveats: a very recent preprint, not yet peer reviewed. It supports rapid flood scenario, forecasting and calibration studies, and relates to the National Water Model record in the catalogue.
